title: Proof-of-Deletion Ledger and Customer Erasure Receipt API
creator: Lena Morrison
description: Build a verifiable, machine-readable proof-of-deletion system and a customer-facing erasure receipt API so customers and auditors can confirm that data subject erasure/RTBF requests were executed according to residency and retention rules. This ticket scopes product requirements, acceptance criteria, and the API contract for the proof attestation service. The system should support hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and produce cryptographically signed deletion attestations, a durable deletion ledger for internal auditors, and an optional customer-facing receipt that can be delivered synchronously or via webhook/email.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/erasure-requests accepts request id, tenant id, scope (user, conversation, tenant), and retention metadata and returns an async job id

Attestation: For completed jobs the system must produce a signed deletion attestation (JSON) containing canonicalized list of deleted object identifiers, timestamps, residency zone, and signing key id
Proof format: Attestations must include a digest and optional Merkle root to enable compact verification for large batches
Customer receipt: Console or API must be able to retrieve a PDF/JSON receipt for a given request id with an embedded signed attestation
Evidence ledger: Internal audit ledger must store immutable records for 7 years by default (configurable per-account) with per-record retention and access controls
Cross-region: Deletions must respect geofenced residency (no evidence exported outside allowed zones) and receipts must include residency metadata
Verification endpoints: GET /v1/erasure-requests/:id/attestation must return verifiable payload and public key metadata; verification should be possible offline given the public key
Observability: Console shows request status, throughput, last 90-day deletion volume, and SLOs (time-to-delete percentiles) for enterprise customers
Security review: Feature must pass security and legal review and include KMS/HSM signing integration and key-rotation plan
E2E tests: Automated tests that submit requests, run purge pipeline, and validate attestation contents across hosted/dedicated/private modes
comments: 2026-03-02 - PM kickoff: Alignment with Legal and Security. Legal flagged need to capture residency claims in the attestation. Action: include explicit residency field and references to retention policy for the tenant.

2026-03-04 - Eng sync: Proposed architecture: lightweight verification microservice, append-only ledger (immutable blob store + manifest) and KMS-signed attestations. Trade-off: full blockchain vs signed Merkle manifests. Decided to implement signed Merkle manifests for compact proofs and lower ops cost.

2026-03-06 - Design feedback: UX for the console receipt workflow needs a modal with receipt preview, reason, and 'download evidence' CTA. Also add rate-limiting info and legal text about verification validity window.

2026-03-09 - Security review draft: Require KMS-backed signing (cloud KMS / HSM for private), certificate rotation schedule, and offline verification keys. Also require tamper-evident ledger storage (WORM-like) for hosted tenants.

2026-03-11 - Eng update: PoC created (github.com/redwood-inference/proof-of-deletion/tree/poC) with a prototype service that emits JSON attestations signed with a test key. Next: integrate with purge engine and add residency enforcement checks.

2026-03-12 - PM note: Need customer-facing contract language for receipts. Draft in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/PoD+-+Erasure+Receipts. Also add compliance partner review for EU GDPR auditors.

2026-03-13 - Ops/Infra: Discussed durability SLAs for the ledger; recommendation is to store attestations in immutable object storage with multi-region replication (subject to residency rules). Action item: ENG-21745 to evaluate storage backends.
2026-03-14 - Current blockers: Private deployment HSM integration and legal sign-off on receipt wording. Blocker tickets: ENG-21745, LEG-96. Working on timelines for resolution.
